situation: Siblings sorting out their late mother's paperwork.
topic: How long do you have to register a death in England?

text: Quick one, does anyone know how long we have to register mum's death in England? The funeral director said "soon" which is no help 🙏
Ngl no idea. I thought it was a few days but could be wrong
@claude how long do you have to register a death in England

Within 5 days in England. That includes weekends, and it's counted from when the death was certified. If the coroner is involved, the timing is different. I couldn't open the GOV.UK page to confirm, so check www.gov.uk/register-a-death. You'll usually need to book an appointment at the register office.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/after-a-death

Rang register office. It's the district where she died, not where she lived. They can do Thurs 10:30 or next Tues. Booked Thurs
They want the GP's medical cert, her NHS number and ID for whoever's registering. Ours only if we're the ones doing it
They said video or phone is fine now if nobody can get there

I couldn't confirm that video registration is allowed. Susan's register office told her it is, but I found no national rule saying so. Shropshire's council page says the law doesn't allow remote registration by phone, email or online, and Tower Hamlets says it doesn't offer video. Before anyone cancels travel, ask Susan to get the Thursday office to confirm it in writing. Otherwise someone could give a declaration at a closer register office.

Sources: https://next.shropshire.gov.uk/births-deaths-and-ceremonies/deaths/registering-a-death
